## Explanatory Data Analysis

This is the explanatory data section. In this section we will look at the explore the images. The goal of this section is to look at the images and try to establish if there are any differences between people, digits, and sessions.

```{r}
#| include: false
display_image <- function(image, title = "") {
  
  if (length(dim(image)) == 3) {
    image <- image[, , 1]
  }
  
  image(
    t(apply(image, 2, rev)),
    col = gray.colors(256),
    axes = FALSE,
    main = title
  )
}
```

### Compare the variation between the people

Firstly, we will compare all 20 peoples handwriting across one session. The main goal of this exercise is to check whether there are any visible variations among peoples handwriting within a particular session. The first image will compare the people writing the digit 0 in session 1.

```{r}
#| include: false
people_examples <- data$metadata %>%
  filter(
    digit == 0,
    session == 1
  ) %>%
  group_by(person_id) %>%
  slice_sample(n = 1) %>%
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
par(
  mfrow = c(4, 5),
  mar = c(1, 1, 2, 1)
)

for (i in 1:nrow(people_examples)) {
  
  image_id <- people_examples$image_id[i]
  person <- people_examples$person_id[i]
  
  display_image(
    data$images[image_id,,,],
    paste("Person", person)
  )
}

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

From the image above we can see that there are different variations in the way people write the digit zero in the first session. Some peoples zeros are more elongated while others look more rounded. The size of the digit differs from person to person. The digits are tilted in different directions, some peoples zero are tilted to the left while others are tilted to the right.

For a more accurate prediction we will compare the between person variation for a different image in the same session. For this we will now compare the between person variation in session one for the digit 1.

### Comparing the digits within people

The next thing we will explore is if there is variation within a persons handwriting. To do this we will randomly select 3 people and we will compare their handwriting across the five different sessions. This particular section is important because later we will build a Siamese network that will compare whether two images were written by the same person or not. A preliminary analysis will visually help us determine if there are similarities within a persons handwriting.

#### Person 1

```{r}

session_examples <- data$metadata %>%
```

### Comparing the digits of the same person

Finally, we will assess the within person variation of the different digits. The main goal of this is to assess whether there are similarities between a persons handwriting for different digits. This section is important because the Siamese and CNN networks will be tasked identifying similarities within the different digits.

For this section we will use the same three people from the previous section. We will keep the session constant and we will assess them on session one.

#### Person 1

### Overall Comments

Visual analysis indicates noticeable variations in handwriting across different individuals. Even when writing the same digit, writers demonstrate distinct differences in shape, scale, stroke direction, and style. However, individual handwriting also displays consistent stylistic patterns; as shown in the previous section, a single writer often applies similar structural and graphical characteristics across different digits.

# CNN


# Siamese neural network


```{r}

set.seed(25)

# output are the indices of the images in each pair
make_pairs <- function(ids, n, person_labels = person_id, digit_labels = digit) {
  
  # Select first image in each pair, allow each image to be in multiple pairs
  a <- sample(ids, n, replace = TRUE)
  
  # Select second image
  b <- vapply(a,
              function(i) {
                # Decide if same or diff writer (50% chance)
                same_writer <- runif(1) < 0.5
                
                if (same_writer) { 
                  
                  # find inds of same writer AND same digit 
                  pool <- ids[person_labels[ids] == person_labels[i] & 
                                digit_labels[ids] == digit_labels[i]]
                  
                } else {
                  
                  # find inds of different writer BUT same digit
                  pool <- ids[person_labels[ids] != person_labels[i] & 
                                digit_labels[ids] == digit_labels[i]]
                }
                
                # Do not pair an image with itself
                # extract all unique image indices excluding the ind of the first image
                pool <- setdiff(pool, i)
                
                # pick 1 to be the second image
                sample(pool, 1)
              },
              integer(1)
  )
  
  cbind(a, b)
}



set.seed(25)
train_pairs <- make_pairs(ids = train_ids, n = 12000)

set.seed(25)
valid_pairs <- make_pairs(ids = valid_ids, n = 4000)

# will use more indepth test pairs, created later
#set.seed(25)
#test_pairs <- make_pairs(ids = test_ids, n = 4000)




make_batch <- function(pair_indices) {
  
  # y = 1 if same writer
  # y = 0 if different writer
  
  y <- matrix(
    as.integer(
      person_id[pair_indices[, 1]] ==
        person_id[pair_indices[, 2]]
    ),
    ncol = 1
  )
  
  list(
    left = images[pair_indices[, 1], , , , drop = FALSE], #first image
    right = images[pair_indices[, 2], , , , drop = FALSE], #second image
    y = y,                                                # same or diff writer
    digit = digit[pair_indices[, 1]],                   # digit in image
    session_left = session[pair_indices[, 1]],         #session of first image
    session_right = session[pair_indices[, 2]]          # session of second
  )
}


train <- make_batch(train_pairs)
#check all digits are same in each pair
all(data$metadata$digit[train_pairs[, 1]] == 
      data$metadata$digit[train_pairs[, 2]])


valid <- make_batch(valid_pairs)
#check for same digits
all(data$metadata$digit[valid_pairs[, 1]] ==
      data$metadata$digit[valid_pairs[, 2]])
```

```{r}

#loss function (y = 1 means same writer) 
contrastive_loss <- function(y, distance) {
  op_mean(y * op_square(distance) + (1 - y) * op_square(op_maximum(
    1 - distance,0)))
}


# calc balanceed accuracy
balanced_accuracy_at <- function(cut) {
  predicts_same <- valid_distance < cut
  same_rate <- mean(predicts_same[valid_same])
  different_rate <- mean(!predicts_same[!valid_same])
  (same_rate + different_rate) / 2
}

```


```{r}
build_siamese <- function(train, valid,
                          n_filters = 16,
                          kernel_size = 3,
                          act_func1 = "relu",
                          act_func2 = "relu",
                          nu = 0.001,
                          dropout_rate = 0.2,
                          n_epochs = 15,
                          lr = 1e-3,
                          double_layer = TRUE,
                          seed = 8) {
  
  # set seed first -----------
  set_random_seed(seed)
  
  # Build CNN ----------------------------
  
  image_input <- layer_input(shape = c(28, 28, 1))
  
  # First convolutional layer
  embedding <- image_input |>
    layer_conv_2d(
      filters = n_filters,
      kernel_size = kernel_size,
      activation = act_func1,
      kernel_regularizer = regularizer_l2(nu)
    ) |>
    layer_max_pooling_2d(pool_size = 2) |>
    layer_dropout(rate = dropout_rate)
  
  # Optional second convolutional layer
  if (double_layer) {
    embedding <- embedding |>
      layer_conv_2d(
        filters = 2 * n_filters,
        kernel_size = kernel_size,
        activation = act_func2,
        kernel_regularizer = regularizer_l2(nu)
      )
  }
  
  # Global average pooling and embedding
  embedding <- embedding |>
    layer_global_average_pooling_2d() |>
    layer_dense(
      units = 16,
      kernel_regularizer = regularizer_l2(nu)
    )
  
  # Package encoder together
  encoder <- keras_model(
    inputs = image_input,
    outputs = embedding
  )
  
  
  # Siamese model ------------------------
  
  left_input <- layer_input(shape = c(28, 28, 1))
  right_input <- layer_input(shape = c(28, 28, 1))
  
  # Encode both images using the same encoder
  distance <- list(
    encoder(left_input),
    encoder(right_input)
  ) |>
    layer_lambda(
      f = function(z) {
        op_sqrt(
          op_sum(
            op_square(z[[1]] - z[[2]]),
            axis = 2,
            keepdims = TRUE
          ) + 1e-7
        )
      }
    )
  
  # Package Siamese model
  siamese_model <- keras_model(
    inputs = list(left_input, right_input),
    outputs = distance
  )
  
  
  # Compile model ------------------------
  
  siamese_model |>
    compile(
      optimizer = optimizer_adam(learning_rate = lr),
      loss = contrastive_loss
    )
  
  
  # Train Siamese model ------------------
  
  history <- siamese_model |>
    fit(
      x = list(train$left, train$right),
      y = train$y,
      validation_data = list(
        list(valid$left, valid$right),
        valid$y
      ),
      epochs = n_epochs,
      batch_size = 64
    )
  
  
  # Validation distances -----------------
  
  valid_distance <- as.numeric(
    predict(
      siamese_model,
      list(valid$left, valid$right)
    )
  )
  
  valid_same <- as.logical(valid$y[, 1])
  
  
  # Find appropriate threshold -----------
  
  threshold_candidates <- sort(unique(valid_distance))
  
  # Calculate balanced accuracy using the
  # previously defined function
  threshold_scores <- vapply(
    threshold_candidates,
    function(cut) {
      predicts_same <- valid_distance < cut
      
      same_rate <- mean(predicts_same[valid_same])
      different_rate <- mean(!predicts_same[!valid_same])
      
      (same_rate + different_rate) / 2
    },
    numeric(1)
  )
  
  best_index <- which.max(threshold_scores)
  threshold <- threshold_candidates[best_index]
  
  
  # Validation results -------------------
  
  validation_result <- data.frame(
    threshold = threshold,
    balanced_accuracy = threshold_scores[best_index]
  )
  
  
  # Return results -----------------------
  
  return(list(
    encoder = encoder,
    siamese_model = siamese_model,
    history = history,
    valid_distance = valid_distance,
    valid_same = valid_same,
    threshold = threshold,
    validation_result = validation_result
  ))
}
######--------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

```{r}

# Hyperparameter grid ----------------------------

# Overall grid not used for tuning
overall_grid <- expand.grid(
  n_filters = c(16, 32, 64),
  kernel_size = c(3, 5, 7),
  act_func1 = c("relu", "tanh"),
  act_func2 = c("relu", "tanh"),
  nu = c(0, 0.001, 0.01),
  dropout_rate = c(0, 0.2, 0.4),
  lr = c(0.01, 0.001, 0.0001),
  KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)



grid_act_funcs <- expand.grid(
  act_func1 = c("relu", "tanh"),
  act_func2 = c("relu", "tanh"),
  KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Seeds for 3 repetitions
seeds <- c(8, 10, 27)

# Store average results for each combination
tuning_act_funcs_balanced_acc <- numeric(nrow(grid_act_funcs))
tuning_act_funcs_val_loss <- numeric(nrow(grid_act_funcs))

# Run each combination 3 times
for (i in seq_len(nrow(grid_act_funcs))) {
  
  cat("-------------Model", i, "of", nrow(grid_act_funcs), "-------------\n")
  
  ba_reps <- numeric(length(seeds))
  loss_reps <- numeric(length(seeds))
  
  for (j in seq_along(seeds)) {
    
    cat("Repetition", j, "of", length(seeds),
        "(seed =", seeds[j], ")\n")
    
    result <- build_siamese(
      train = train,
      valid = valid,
      act_func1 = grid_act_funcs$act_func1[i],
      act_func2 = grid_act_funcs$act_func2[i],
      seed = seeds[j]
    )
    
    ba_reps[j] <- as.numeric(
      result$validation_result[2]
    )
    
    loss_reps[j] <- as.numeric(
      tail(result$history$metrics$val_loss, 1)
    )
  }
  
  # Average across the 3 repetitions
  tuning_act_funcs_balanced_acc[i] <- mean(ba_reps)
  tuning_act_funcs_val_loss[i] <- mean(loss_reps)
}

# Create results data frame (same structure as before)
tuning_act_funcs_df <- as.data.frame(
  rbind(
    tuning_act_funcs_balanced_acc,
    tuning_act_funcs_val_loss
  )
)

# column and row names
colnames(tuning_act_funcs_df) <- c("relu_relu", "tanh_relu", "relu_tanh", "tanh_tanh")

rownames(tuning_act_funcs_df) <- c("Balanced accuracy", "Validation loss")
```

```{r siamese-filter-tune}



grid_filter <- expand.grid(
  n_filters = c(16, 32, 64),
  kernel_size = c(3, 5, 7),
  KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Store results
grid_filter_results <- grid_filter
grid_filter_results$balanced_accuracy <- NA_real_
grid_filter_results$val_loss <- NA_real_

# Run each combination 3 times
seeds <- c(8, 10, 27)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(grid_filter))) {
  cat('=================== Model', i, 'of', nrow(grid_filter), ' ===================\n')
  
  # Store metrics for the 3 repetitions
  ba_reps <- numeric(length(seeds))
  loss_reps <- numeric(length(seeds))
  
  for (j in seq_along(seeds)) {
    cat('---------- Repetition', j, 'of', length(seeds),
        '(seed =', seeds[j], ') ----------\n')
    
    result <- build_siamese(
      train = train,
      valid = valid,
      act_func1 = act_func1,
      act_func2 = act_func2,
      n_filters = grid_filter$n_filters[i],
      kernel_size = grid_filter$kernel_size[i],
      double_layer = TRUE,
      seed = seeds[j]
    )
    
    ba_reps[j] <- result$validation_result$balanced_accuracy
    loss_reps[j] <- tail(result$history$metrics$val_loss, 1)
  }
  
  # Average metrics across the 3 repetitions
  grid_filter_results$balanced_accuracy[i] <- mean(ba_reps)
  grid_filter_results$val_loss[i] <- mean(loss_reps)
}

# View results (same structure as before)
grid_filter_results
```

```{r}

# create different pairs for test set
set.seed(25)

# All test images are from session 5
test_ids <- which(data$metadata$session == 5)

# Function to create controlled test pairs
make_controlled_pairs <- function(ids, n, pair_type) {
  
  pairs <- matrix(NA_integer_, nrow = n, ncol = 2)
  
  for (j in 1:n) {
    
    # Choose first image
    i <- sample(ids, 1)
    
    person_i <- person_id[i]
    digit_i <- digit[i]
    session_i <- session[i]
    
    if (pair_type == "same_writer_same_session") {
      
      pool <- ids[person_id[ids] == person_i & digit[ids] == digit_i 
                  & session[ids] == session_i & ids != i]
      
    } else if (pair_type == "same_writer_different_session") {
      
      # For cross-session pairs, use sessions 1-4
      comparison_ids <- which(person_id == person_i & digit == digit_i 
                              & session != session_i)
      
      pool <- comparison_ids[comparison_ids %in% 
                               c(which(session %in% c(1, 2, 3, 4)))]
      
    } else if (pair_type == "different_writer_same_session") {
      
      pool <- ids[person_id[ids] != person_i & digit[ids] == digit_i 
                  & session[ids] == session_i]
      
    } else if (pair_type == "different_writer_different_session") {
      
      # different session, therefore allow sessions 1 to 4 again
      comparison_ids <- which(person_id != person_i & digit == digit_i 
                              & session != session_i 
                              & session %in% c(1, 2, 3, 4))
      
      pool <- comparison_ids
      
    }
    
    pairs[j, ] <- c(i, sample(pool, 1))
  }
  
  pairs
}




# use functin to get different types of test pairs
n_per_type <- 1000

set.seed(25)
test_pairs_same_same <- make_controlled_pairs(test_ids, n_per_type, 
                                              "same_writer_same_session")

set.seed(25)
test_pairs_same_diff <- make_controlled_pairs(test_ids, n_per_type,
                                              "same_writer_different_session")

set.seed(25)
test_pairs_diff_same <- make_controlled_pairs(test_ids, n_per_type,
                                              "different_writer_same_session")

set.seed(25)
test_pairs_diff_diff <- make_controlled_pairs(test_ids, n_per_type, 
                                              "different_writer_different_session")


# combine
test_pairs <- rbind(test_pairs_same_same,test_pairs_same_diff,
                    test_pairs_diff_same,test_pairs_diff_diff)

dim(test_pairs)


test_pair_type <- c(
  rep("Same writer, same session", n_per_type),
  rep("Same writer, different session", n_per_type),
  rep("Different writer, same session", n_per_type),
  rep("Different writer, different session", n_per_type)
)

#table(test_pair_type)

test <- make_batch(test_pairs)
test$pair_type <- test_pair_type


# check pairs are of correct formats, combinations
table(test_pair_type, person_id[test_pairs[,1]] == person_id[test_pairs[,2]])

all(digit[test_pairs[,1]] == digit[test_pairs[,2]])

table(test_pair_type, session[test_pairs[,1]] == session[test_pairs[,2]])

######--------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

```{r}
  keep <- session_type == s

  pred_s <- predicted_same[keep]
  
  sensitivity_s <- mean(pred_s[true_s])
  
  specificity_s <- mean(!pred_s[!true_s])
  
  data.frame(
    session_type = s,
    n = sum(keep),
    accuracy = mean(pred_s == true_s),
    sensitivity = sensitivity_s,
    specificity = specificity_s,
    balanced_accuracy = (sensitivity_s + specificity_s) / 2)
})
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Find one incorrect prediction per writer-session category and one per digit

set.seed(25)

# Identify incorrectly classified pairs
incorrect <- which(predicted_same != true_same)

# Select one random incorrect pair from a set of rows
choose_error <- function(rows, category, value) {
  
  errors <- rows[rows %in% incorrect]
  
  if (length(errors) == 0) {
    message("No incorrect predictions for: ", category, " = ", value)
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  selected <- sample(errors, 1)
  
  data.frame(
    row = selected,
    category = category,
    value = as.character(value)
  )
}

# One example for each writer-session combination
pair_types <- c("Same writer, same session",
  "Same writer, different session",
  "Different writer, same session",
  "Different writer, different session")

writer_session_examples <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pair_types, function(p) {
  choose_error(which(test_pair_type == p), "Writer-session", p)
}))

# One example for each digit
digit_examples <- do.call(rbind, lapply(0:4, function(d) {
  choose_error(which(test$digit == d), "Digit", d)
}))

# Combine the selected examples
examples <- do.call(rbind, Filter(Negate(is.null),
  list(writer_session_examples, digit_examples)))

rownames(examples) <- NULL

# Summarise the incorrect predictions -----------------------

example_details <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(examples)), function(j) {
  
  r <- examples$row[j]
  i <- test_pairs[r, 1]
  k <- test_pairs[r, 2]
  
  data.frame(
    category = examples$category[j],
    value = examples$value[j],
    pair_row = r,
    digit = digit[i],
    writer_left = person_id[i],
    session_left = session[i],
    writer_right = person_id[k],
    session_right = session[k],
    true_label = ifelse(true_same[r], "Same writer", "Different writers"),
    predicted_label = ifelse(
      predicted_same[r], "Same writer", "Different writers"
    ),
    distance = test_distance[r]
  )
}))

print(example_details, row.names = FALSE)

# Plot the two images in each selected pair -------------------------


plot_pair_example <- function(r, heading = "") {
  
  i <- test_pairs[r, 1]
  k <- test_pairs[r, 2]
  
  # Extract each 28 x 28 image
  img_left <- images[i, , , 1]
  img_right <- images[k, , , 1]
  
  # True and predicted labels
  actual <- ifelse(true_same[r], "Same writer", "Different writers")
  predicted <- ifelse(
    predicted_same[r], "Same writer", "Different writers"
  )
  
  # Display images side by side
  old_par <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1), oma = c(0, 0, 2, 0))
  
  image(
    x = 1:28, y = 1:28,
    z = t(img_left[28:1, ]),
    col = gray.colors(256, start = 0, end = 1),
    axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "", asp = 1,
    main = paste0("Writer ", person_id[i],
                  ", session ", session[i]))
  
  image(
    x = 1:28, y = 1:28,
    z = t(img_right[28:1, ]),
    col = gray.colors(256, start = 0, end = 1),
    axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "", asp = 1,
    main = paste0("Writer ", person_id[k],
                  ", session ", session[k]))
  
  # Centred above both images
  mtext(paste0(heading, "Threshold: ", round(final_siamese$threshold,3), 
               " | True: ", actual, " | Predicted: ", predicted, 
               " | Distance: ", round(test_distance[r], 3)), 
        side = 3, outer = TRUE, line = 0.5, cex = 0.9)
  
  par(old_par)
}

# Plot each selected examples

for (j in seq_len(nrow(examples))) {
  image_name <- paste0("siamese_error", j, ".png")
  png(filename = image_name, width = 1200, height = 600, res = 150)
  
  plot_pair_example(
    examples$row[j])
  dev.off()
}
```
